page: Microsoft Azure EC2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 1 physical core presenting 2 dedicated virtual cores (vCPUs) via simultaneous multithreading. The system includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It provides 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with no GPU included, while 81 GB of local SSD storage is directly bundled.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate average single-threaded baseline performance alongside constrained multi-threaded execution due to the 2-vCPU configuration. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1181.0 (average) and a multi-core score of 1415.0 (bottom 10%). A similar trend appears in stress-ng CPU measurements, scoring 1982.37 in both single-core (average) and multi-core (bottom 10%) workloads. PassMark metrics indicate a CPU score of 2353.04, an extended instructions score of 1484.19, a physics score of 266.27, and a database operations score of 724.95, each placing in the bottom 10%. Memory subsystem throughput yielded a PassMark memory score of 1481.53 (weak), while Redis SET throughput reached 1.69 million operations per second (bottom 10%).

Given its high RAM allocation relative to core count and bundled fast local scratch storage, the EC2ads_v5 is positioned for lightweight memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel compute capacity. It is suited for small in-memory caches, development database instances, lightweight Redis deployments, and memory-intensive background utilities requiring local temporary storage.
description: Microsoft Azure EC2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor under Microsoft Hyper-V. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core, 16.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per vCPU), and 81 GB of bundled local SSD storage, without a GPU. The architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache, AVX, and AES instructions. In synthetic benchmarks, it exhibits average single-core throughput (Geekbench single-core score of 1181.0, stress-ng single-core score of 1982.37) but lower overall multi-threaded capacity due to its two-thread limit, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 1415.0 and Redis SET throughput of 1.69 million operations per second. The high 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and direct local disk make it suited for small memory-intensive workloads, including lightweight in-memory databases, local caching, and non-parallelized analytical tasks.
